title: Students and professors protest Palestinian activist's arrest in Jerusalem

tea.why: Protesters gathered outside the Jerusalem District Court to oppose the administrative detention of a Hebrew University student.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded the immediate release of the detained student.
tea.changed: Nov 24: The Jerusalem District Court held a further hearing on the administrative detention of the student, while about 200 demonstrators gathered outside.

summary: Students, professors, and activists gathered outside the Jerusalem District Court during a hearing concerning the administrative detention of a Hebrew University student. Organised by groups including Standing Together alongside Jewish and Arab student representatives, the protest called for the release of the 26-year-old sociology and criminology student who was arrested earlier in the month at the Mount Scopus dormitories. Authorities are seeking to hold him for six months without charge or trial, alleging a connection to a terrorist act in an investigation with the Shin Bet. Meanwhile, organizers and representatives accused authorities of politically motivated detention, mistreatment, and physical abuse during the arrest, claims that were contested by police who stated he resisted arrest.
response: Police stated the student was arrested under a court-issued warrant on suspicion of a connection to a terrorist act in an investigation with the Shin Bet, and that he resisted arrest and received legal advice.

updates.text: The Jerusalem District Court held a hearing regarding the administrative detention as about 200 demonstrators gathered outside.
